review.method: 对照所列资料中的相关事实，目视检查源 PNG 及转换后的 WebP；结构示意不按比例。

checks: 掌部放大图的五个常规趾和爪可辨认，未把伪拇指画成同排第六根长指。
伪拇指标注指向腕部的局部示意，而非趾尖。
前掌夹竹子的场景与臼齿压碎食物的示意分开，未表达完整齿列。
limitations: 尚未独立专业二审或亲子试读。
压缩、哈希和尺寸测试只验证技术属性，不能代替生物学审核。

prompt: Create a polished Chinese children's natural-history teaching illustration for ages 6–12. Landscape 3:2 composition, high resolution. Warm ivory paper background, restrained watercolor + precise fine ink lines, clean museum science-book design, natural proportions, generous whitespace, very clear close-up structures, accurate anatomy, realistic rather than cute cartoon, no anthropomorphic faces, no clothes, no logo, no watermark, no fake photographic or fossil evidence. Large clear simplified-Chinese labels only as specified, no extra title or paragraphs. Diagrams are explanatory schematics, not to scale. Keep everything comfortably inside the canvas, no cropped structures. Subject: Ailuropoda melanoleuca, giant panda. Three clearly separated teaching vignettes: LEFT a natural seated black-and-white panda holding bamboo with normal broad furry bear forepaws, chewing bamboo, full head and forelimbs visible. UPPER RIGHT a large carefully drawn palm/underside schematic of ONE panda forepaw: exactly FIVE short normal claw-bearing toes on the distal edge, broad compact bear paw, NOT a human hand. The enlarged radial sesamoid is a SMALL rounded-oblong bony prominence at the inner WRIST on the radial side, proximal to the toes, offset from the toe row, shown as a muted ochre cutaway beneath a small transparent patch of fur. It opposes the five toes when gripping, NOT a sixth elongated finger; no extra claw on it. A bamboo stalk is gently held between this wrist prominence and the flexed normal digits. A leader clearly points to the wrist prominence with the exact label “伪拇指（腕骨）”. Another leader points to the ordinary toes labelled “五趾”. LOWER RIGHT a simple enlarged isolated posterior bear molar schematic with a broad crushing crown and a green bamboo fragment, not a whole jaw or complete tooth count. Label “臼齿磨碎竹子”. Use the exact separate label “前掌夹住竹子” near the main feeding pose. The wrist bone must not be placed at a fingertip or on the back of the hand. Avoid human palms, six finger hands, six claws, surgical gore, exposed full skeleton.

prompt.prompt: Edit this teaching plate, preserving the panda, forepaw, wrist bone inset, bamboo, all Chinese text, layout and watercolor style. Change ONLY the isolated tooth drawing at LOWER RIGHT. The current tooth looks too much like a square four-cusped human molar. Replace it with a simplified GIANT PANDA POSTERIOR MOLAR CROWN: a broad, distinctly elongated rectangular grinding platform, roughly 1.7 times as long as wide, viewed obliquely from above, with several low rounded enamel cusps and a complex finely ridged/crenulated crushing surface across the length. This represents broad panda cheek teeth adapted to crushing tough bamboo, not a human tooth, not a mastodon tooth, and not a sharp carnivore shearing blade. Show only the crown and a small low base; no long pointed or human-like tooth roots. Add a small green bamboo fragment touching the grinding surface to show the function. Preserve exact label 臼齿磨碎竹子, make its fine leader end on the crown. Keep upper right forepaw with FIVE ordinary toes and the small radial sesamoid at the wrist exactly as before, NOT a sixth finger. Do not alter other vignettes or text.
